summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with leg edema, dysuria, and left lower quadrant abdominal pain. Evaluation confirmed signs of a urinary tract infection on urinalysis, though the urine culture later showed no growth, likely due to early antibiotic treatment. The abdominal pain was attributed to panniculitis, and she was treated with IV ceftriaxone followed by oral Keflex. Volume overload was managed with IV furosemide, and she responded well with improved symptoms and stable renal function. Her chronic conditions, including HIV on suppressive therapy, diastolic heart failure, obstructive sleep apnea, and chronic pain, were maintained on home regimens. A pressure ulcer on the left leg was noted, and wound care was consulted. She was discharged home on her baseline medications, including Coumadin with close INR monitoring, and new prescriptions for Keflex and topical antifungal/barrier creams for skin care. Follow-up was arranged for INR, weight monitoring, and mental health support.
